spec_match.rationale: Maps each §3.1.6 tabs-mode behaviour (implicit roles, roving tabindex, arrow keys, pruning, focus-scope ownership) to the exact line of ARIA/JS it replaces, with both implementations live on the page.

interactive.rationale: The hand-rolled ARIA widget is fully operational everywhere — click, ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End, roving tabindex, hidden toggling, aria-live state readout — beside the scrollable CSS tabs-mode widget.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a working roving-tabindex widget next to the CSS equivalent with a line-by-line accounting; the page contains both plus the deletion table.

edge_cases.rationale: The migration table covers each behaviour class and the pre-modes fallback is explained, but wrap-around arrow behaviour differences and RTL arrow-key direction are not demonstrated.

references.rationale: chromestatus entry, the spec modes section and the WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern are linked.

conformance.rationale: The suite's manual tabs-mode-aria-contract assertion is the formal statement of what this migration deletes; the grammar assertions pin the declaration the CSS half uses.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141: autorun programmatically selected the Activity tab and the assert verified aria-selected/hidden flipped (screenshot shows Activity dark, its panel shown, readout updated); desktop and emulated-mobile captures show both halves rendering without overlap after the marker-strip height fix; console clean. The ARIA half — the half that must work today — is fully exercised.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the support probe, the fallback branch, and the autorun ARIA state transition (aria-selected + hidden consistency).

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; aria-selected and :target-current states both invert background and color; tab buttons override the global button background with color set alongside.

accessibility.rationale: The ARIA half implements the APG tabs pattern faithfully (roles, roving tabindex, keyboard handler, labelled panels, aria-live state text); the CSS half's semantics are delegated to the mode and honestly bannered on pre-modes browsers.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, halves stack, tabs keep 44px height, no console errors.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Custom tab widgets need the full APG contract: roles, aria-selected, roving tabindex, arrow-key support and hidden inactive panels.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The left-hand widget implements that contract completely (it is the page's baseline artifact), and the deletion table enumerates each requirement against the mode keyword that absorbs it.

guidanceConsulted.query: CSS-only carousel with scroll markers tabs accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer platform-provided semantics over scripted ARIA when an equivalent native mechanism exists.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: That is the migration's thesis; the page still ships the scripted version as the working baseline for pre-154 browsers rather than removing it.

openQuestions.title: Side-by-side screen-reader transcript on Chrome 154
openQuestions.detail: Once a modes-enabled build is available, capture the accessibility-tree/screen-reader announcements for both halves and note any divergence (e.g. whether the UA exposes position-in-set for markers the way aria-setsize does for the scripted version). Divergences would be exactly the migration caveats developers need.

summary: Migration study: a complete, working WAI-ARIA tabs widget beside its CSS tabs-mode replacement, with a behaviour-by-behaviour deletion table. The scripted half was fully exercised headless (autorun state transition asserted, keyboard handler in place); the CSS half renders with an honest pre-modes banner on Chromium 141.
